verdict: A quiet day: mostly arXiv paper churn and AWN press-release filler, with a couple of ComfyUI/MiniMax-H3 tool drops the only items worth a working TD's ten minutes.

stories.headline: MiniMax-H3 video model gets ComfyUI workflows and LoRA speed/detail sliders
stories.body: Two community releases around MiniMax-H3: a ComfyUI workflow package (javawock7618) supporting first/last-frame bridging, reference-to-video and ControlNet-Union, plus a LoRA (siraxe) adding speed and detail sliders on top of the base model via diffusers. Both are community uploads on Hugging Face, not vendor-official tooling; download counts are low to moderate (6392 for the LoRA) and no VRAM or licence figures are given.
stories.why: First/last-frame and ControlNet support in ComfyUI is the kind of thing that turns into a pipeline node quickly.

stories.headline: Framestore builds in-house AI tools for Sky Christmas campaign VFX
stories.body: Framestore's 'That's Christmas Sorted' for Sky Creative used new internally built AI tools alongside standard CG pipeline work: previs assistance, character removal, and self-animating costume effects. CG warehouse environments were built conventionally. Details are limited to AWN's trade coverage; no specifics on which models, software, or whether any of it is shared outside the studio.
stories.why: A tier-one facility shipping bespoke AI tooling into a real delivery is a signal worth tracking, even if details are thin.
